record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: For any even positive integer k, does there exist an ℓ-group admitting exactly k distinct lattice orders?

evidence.quote: 1.6. For any even positive integer k, does there exist an ℓ-group admitting exactly k distinct lattice orders? (cf. Problem 3.24)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) is a group G equipped with a partial order ≤ such that (G, ≤) is a lattice and the group multiplication is order-preserving on both sides, i.e. a ≤ b implies xay ≤ xby for all x, y ∈ G. Two lattice orders ≤₁ and ≤₂ on the same group G are considered distinct if they determine different positive cones {g ∈ G : g ≥ e}.

Question: For every even positive integer k, does there exist a group G that admits exactly k distinct lattice orders making it an ℓ-group?
